evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: This would take within the next five to ten minutes of your time so we can be able to build an accurate code. You can depend on. Would that be okay? — Rep does wait for yes, but frames it as '5 to 10 minutes' not the standard '10 to 15 minutes,' and delivery is awkward/transcription-garbled.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Do you have any concerns or any important things that you wanted to answer during this call today? — Asked early, but immediately after opening framing, before the rep actually paused or confirmed the customer understood the process. Asked before logistics probing begins.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer states 'I don't want to have a minimum number of hours in the company because I, it's kind of a small move.' Rep responds with immediate explanation of the 2.5-hour minimum instead of asking 'tell me more about that' or 'what is it about the minimum that concerns you.' No follow-up depth on the stated concern.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: No summary or reflection of the customer's concern about minimums. Rep pivots directly to explaining policy.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Rep covers: property type (condo), floor/stories (2 floors at origin, 1 story at destination), rooms (bedroom, garage identified), walk distance (20 feet), additional rooms (garage), special considerations (items split between floors), second stop confirmed. All seven probing items addressed despite customer's resistance to square footage.
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: Not mentioned at any point in the call.
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Not asked. Customer explicitly stated 'I don't have any boxes, I just have furniture,' but rep did not ask about typical box count or overflow risk.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Typical one bedroom appointment would normally takes two movers. That's between two and a half to three and a half hours to complete. In your case... two movers and one truck estimated time is between three and a half to four and a half hours. The estimated cost would be $1,060. — Full anchoring with typical range + personalization to this customer's specific move size and prep needs.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Early rate of 105 dollars per hour per mover... trip fee of 115 dollars... minimum of two and a half hours... it will always be prorated to fifteen minute increments. — All key elements disclosed: hourly rate, trip fee, minimum, increments. Full disclosure before customer asks.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Rep never asked 'Does that feel fair?' or any variant. Moved directly from estimate explanation into booking language without soliciting customer reaction to price.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: if you cannot make it to the time window that we arrange, we immediately start discounting money of your final bill. — Fully delivered with discount mechanism clear.
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: we have no worry, damage coverage included on the already weight that you're paying us. We will provide up to 2000 dollars per move. That is to repair, replace and reimburse for your items. — Covers $2,000, mentions 'included,' but does NOT explicitly state 'no deductible' or 'no fine print' framing that the rubric specifies.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: Rep does not ask 'Does that put those to rest?' or equivalent. Instead moves directly to booking discussion without confirming the two promises addressed the customer's original concern (the minimum hours).
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Not asked. Rep moves from pricing straight into booking without a 'What's still concerning you?' question.
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: Not asked. No 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?' variant.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Would you like our help with your move? — Asked plainly and clearly with no softened out. However, customer deflects ('I'll keep this information I'm interviewing several companies') and rep never re-asks or confirms intent, so the ask registers but is not acted upon.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: No mention of rate lock. Rep does mention 'no deposit required' but not that the quote itself is locked or good for a specific period.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Partial. Date (October 25th) and time window (8:30–9:00 AM) confirmed. No phone number, crew size, or moving day address re-confirmation captured after customer deflects. No notes left for crew about the customer's concern (minimum hours). Customer does not commit, so full booking details were never finalized.

top_strength: Excellent logistics detail gathering—rep systematically extracted all seven logistics items (property types, floors, room counts, walk distance, additional stops, special considerations) despite the customer's initial resistance to providing square footage.
coaching_note: Never asked 'Does that feel fair?' after pricing, did not probe the customer's stated concern about minimums beyond one explanation, and abandoned the close entirely when the customer deflected—no re-ask, no commitment, no final confirmation.
